{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# Python: "3.10" "3.11" "3.12"
# Older versions than 3.8 do not support f-strings
# Older versions than 3.10 do not support Numpy 2


name: Python package

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [ deploy ]
  # pull_request:
  #   branches: [ deploy ]

jobs:

  # # Does not produce manylinux that is required for twine
  # build_unix:
  #   name: Build wheels on ${{ matrix.os }}
  #   runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
  #   strategy:
  #     fail-fast: true
  #     matrix:
  #       # os: [ubuntu-20.04,ubuntu-18.04]
  #       # python-version: ["3.8","3.9","3.10"]
  #       os: [ubuntu-18.04]
  #       python-version: ["3.9"]
  #   steps:
  #   - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  #   - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
  #     uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  #     with:
  #       python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
  #   - name: Install dependencies
  #     run: |
  #       python -m pip install --upgrade pip
  #       python -m pip install pytest pytest-benchmark build
  #       python -m pip install numpy scipy matplotlib>=3.0.0
  #       if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
  #   - name: Compile and install
  #     run: |
  #       python -m pip install . -v
  #       ls ${{ github.workspace }}/build || true
  #   - name: Test installation
  #     run : |
  #       mv dtaidistance dtaidistance_pkg
  #       python ./util/check_installation.py
  #       mv dtaidistance_pkg dtaidistance
  #   - name: Test with pytest
  #     run: |
  #       mv dtaidistance dtaidistance_pkg
  #       pytest --ignore=venv --benchmark-skip
  #       mv dtaidistance_pkg dtaidistance
  #   - name: Build
  #     run: |
  #       python -m build
  #   - name: Store wheels
  #     uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  #     with:
  #       name: wheels
  #       path: dist/*.whl

  build_unix:
    name: Build wheels on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        # os: [ubuntu-20.04,ubuntu-18.04]
        # python-version: ["3.8","3.9","3.10"]
        os: [ubuntu-22.04]
        # cibuildwheel will automatically provide all Python versions
        python-version: ["3.10"]
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python -m pip install cibuildwheel==2.19.1
    - name: Build wheel
      run: |
        python -m cibuildwheel --output-dir dist/
        ls dist/
      env:
        CIBW_BUILD_VERBOSITY: 2
        # cp36-* and cp37-* do not support f-strings
        CIBW_SKIP: cp36-* cp37-* cp38-* cp39-* pp* *-manylinux_i686 *-musllinux_i686 *-musllinux_x86_64
        CIBW_TEST_EXTRAS: "dev"
        CIBW_TEST_COMMAND: pytest --ignore=venv --benchmark-skip {project}/tests
    - name: Store wheels
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: dist-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
        path: dist/*.whl


  build_macos:
    name: Build wheels on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        # os: [macos-14, macos-14-arm64, macos-15, macos-15-arm64]
        os: [macos-15]  # macos-14 and macos-15 generate a wheel with the same name
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install OpenMP
      run: |
        # OpenMP libraries are not installed by default on macos
        clang --version
        clang --version | grep "\(13\.\|14\.\|15\.\|16\.\)"
        # hardcoded, not ideal
        # https://mac.r-project.org/openmp/
        # This includes only the dynamic library
        curl -O https://mac.r-project.org/openmp/openmp-13.0.0-darwin21-Release.tar.gz
        sudo tar fvxz openmp-13.0.0-darwin21-Release.tar.gz -C /
        ls /usr/local/lib
        ls /usr/local/include
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python -m pip install pytest pytest-benchmark build
        python -m pip install numpy scipy matplotlib>=3.0.0
        if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
    - name: Compile and install
      run: |
        export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"
        export CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include"
        python -m pip install . -v
        ls ${{ github.workspace }}/build || true
    - name: Test installation
      run : |
        python ./util/check_installation.py
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"
        export CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include"
        pytest --ignore=venv --benchmark-skip
    - name: Build
      run: |
        python -m build
        ls dist/
    - name: Store wheels
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: dist-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
        path: dist/*.whl


  build_windows:
    name: Build wheels on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        os: [ windows-2022 ]  # windows-2019 (produces same filenames as 2022)
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python -m pip install pytest pytest-benchmark pytest-env build cython
        python -m pip install numpy scipy matplotlib>=3.0.0
    - name: Compile and install
      run: |
        python -m pip install . -v
        ls ${{ github.workspace }}/build || true
    - name: Test installation
      run : |
        python ./util/check_installation.py
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        pytest --ignore=venv --benchmark-skip -c pytest-noviz.ini
    - name: Build
      run: |
        python -m build
        ls dist/
    - name: Store wheels
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: dist-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
        path: dist/*.whl


  build_sdist:
    name: Prepare source distribution
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
      - name: Build
        run: |
          python -m pip install build
          python -m build --sdist
      - name: Store artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-source
          path: dist/*.tar.gz


  upload_wheels:
    name: Upload wheels to PyPi
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # upload to PyPI on every tag starting with 'v'
    # if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.event.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: [build_unix,build_macos,build_windows,build_sdist]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: dist-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: dist

      - name: Install twine
        run: python -m pip install --upgrade twine

      - name: Check distribution with twine
        run: twine check dist/*

      - name: Publish package to PyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          user: __token__
          password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
          packages_dir: dist/
",
  "rationale": "Add pip dependency caching to all four build jobs (build_unix, build_macos, build_windows, build_sdist) using actions/cache@v4 with a key based on pyproject.toml hash. This optimization is directly supported by experimental evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) showing the same pattern applied to a Python workflow, and by the literature pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE which reports modest aggregate benefits for caching dependency downloads. The workflow currently has no caching, and all jobs perform pip installs that would benefit from cached wheels. The change preserves all build and test coverage, adds no privileged actions, and uses only the existing pyproject.toml as cache key input.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}

The user wants me to analyze the provided workflow and evidence to propose a CI optimization. Let me first understand the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is a Python package build workflow that builds wheels for multiple platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows) using cibuildwheel on Linux and manual builds on macOS/Windows. It also builds a source distribution and uploads to PyPI.

Looking at the evidence, I have several patterns and experiment examples. The most relevant ones seem to be:

1. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) - has experimental evidence showing caching pip dependencies
2. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure) - has experimental evidence
3. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (Bound jobs with a custom timeout) - has experimental evidence
4. P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE (Share cached build dependencies) - has experimental evidence showing pip cache

The workflow currently doesn't have any caching for pip dependencies. The experiment example for P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE shows adding a pip cache step using actions/cache@v4 with path ~/.cache/pip and key based on pyproject.toml hash.

The workflow has multiple jobs (build_unix, build_macos, build_windows, build_sdist) that all install Python dependencies. Adding pip caching could speed up these jobs.

Let me check the workflow for any existing caching - I don't see any cache steps currently.

The evidence from experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2 shows adding a pip cache step to a Python workflow. This is directly applicable.

Also, the pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE from the literature supports caching dependency downloads.

The workflow uses matrix builds for different OS/Python combinations. The fail-fast is already set to true in the strategy, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is already implemented.

For timeouts, the workflow doesn't have explicit timeouts. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT could be applied, but we'd need to know typical run times. The evidence shows 26% savings in one experiment.

Given the evidence, the most directly applicable and well-supported optimization is adding pip caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE / P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE). The experiment example shows exactly how to do this for a Python workflow.

Let me verify the workflow structure - each job that installs dependencies could benefit from caching. The jobs are:
- build_unix: installs cibuildwheel and builds
- build_macos: installs pytest, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, etc.
- build_windows: installs pytest, pytest-benchmark, pytest-env, build, cython, numpy, scipy, matplotlib
- build_sdist: installs build

All of these use pip install, so caching ~/.cache/pip would help.

The experiment example uses:
- path: ~/.cache/pip
- key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
- restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

This is a good pattern. The workflow has pyproject.toml at the root, so hashFiles('pyproject.toml') should work.

I should add this cache step to each job that does pip install, right before the "Install dependencies" step.

Let me also check if there are any contraindications. The pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has contraindications: "Mutable or untrusted cached content" and "An equivalent cache already exists". There's no existing cache, and pip cache is generally safe.

The evidence IDs I can use are:
- experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2 (shows pip caching in a Python workflow)
- pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (literature support for caching dependency downloads)

I'll propose adding pip caching to all four jobs that install dependencies.

Now, I need to produce the updated workflow YAML. Let me construct it carefully.

The workflow is long, so I'll need to add the cache step to each relevant job. Let me identify the exact positions:

1. build_unix job: after "Set up Python" and before "Install dependencies"
2. build_macos job: after "Set up Python" and before "Install dependencies"  
3. build_windows job: after "Set up Python" and before "Install dependencies"
4. build_sdist job: after "Setup Python" and before "Build"

Each cache step should be identical except the job context.

Let me write the updated workflow.
